National Overview

National schools, enrolment and teachers for the selected academic year.
Charts render locally — figures are drawn in the browser from the loaded dashboard data; no external chart library or internet connection is required.
Complete 2011-12 → 2025-26 series. Every year has data for every card and chart. Figures published by the Government of India (UDISE+, Ministry of Education, NITI Aayog, PIB) are kept exactly as published. Where no official figure exists for a year or state, the value is an estimate (linear interpolation between published values, or the nearest published value moved in line with the national trend) and is marked e or * . See Data Sources & Methodology → Data provenance for the exact counts. Estimates are for exploration, not official statistics.
Now multi-year: use the academic-year filter above to update year-aware pages. Dropout, GER, facilities, staffing and national totals are available across different ranges in Multi-Year Data; the Ask the Data page can query the full loaded series.
Scope of this dashboard: It combines the supplied AY2023–24/AY2024–25 state and management extracts with the cleaned multi-year datasets. The year-wise government/private comparison covers every year from 2011–12 through 2025–26. UDISE+ management splits are observed only for 2023–24 and 2024–25 (the latter enrolment split is flagged as suspect); earlier and later splits are explicitly labelled estimates based on the nearest available management shares and national totals. Other measures, including facilities, dropout and GER, are not assigned a school-management split because the source does not report one.

How to read this: Source-reported national totals are allocated using UDISE+ government and private-unaided shares from 2023–24 (and 2024–25 for schools and teachers). Where a total or management split is missing, it is estimated by linear interpolation/extrapolation or by carrying forward the nearest observed share. Estimates are not official UDISE+ management counts. Government Aided and other unallocated schools/students/teachers remain in the “Other / aided” remainder. The AY2024–25 enrolment split is estimated because the supplied management file repeats the previous year’s values.

Single-teacher schools

States with the most single-teacher schools

A single-teacher school has one teacher covering every grade taught there — a direct staffing-strain indicator available in this dataset
Flagged data anomaly: West Bengal's AY2024 row reports 23,549,432 students "enrolled in single-teacher schools" against a state total enrolment of about 17.08 million. This is mathematically impossible, so the suspect field is excluded from cleaned analysis. The original source value is retained in the JSON export for audit rather than guessed or silently discarded.
Pupil–Teacher Ratio (PTR) = Total Students ÷ Total Teachers. A lower PTR means each teacher is, on average, responsible for fewer students. It does not by itself mean better teaching, better infrastructure or better learning outcomes — those require classroom-level and learning-assessment data this dashboard does not have. Treat PTR here as one input into teacher-availability planning, not a quality score.

How this works: questions are grounded in evidence retrieved from the loaded school datasets. With Groq configured, the analyst summarizes that evidence and separates observed facts from recommendations; without the key, the local data answer remains available. Unavailable evidence is never invented.
Update: the evidence summary and any available year-specific comparisons below follow the selected academic year. Dropout, enrolment ratios and facilities can be explored by their reported years in Multi-Year Trends; learning outcomes, fees and other unreported topics are not inferred.
The brief's twelve key research questions are answered only as far as the loaded UDISE+ data allows. Each question includes improvement metrics showing: (1) Current Coverage—how much of the question can be answered with available data; (2) Potential Coverage—what's possible with complete datasets; (3) Possible Gain—the improvement opportunity.
Every insight below is generated from the loaded UDISE+ data only, split into fact (what the data shows), interpretation (a reasonable reading of it) and recommendation (what to investigate or do next) — kept deliberately separate so an interpretation is never mistaken for a fact, and a recommendation is never mistaken for something the data proved.

Definitions used in this dashboard

GovernmentSchools UDISE+ classifies under state/central government management. Reported as a single "Government" figure in the national file; the state-wise file does not split by management, so no state-wise government count exists in this data.
Government AidedPrivately managed but government-aided schools, kept as its own category throughout — never merged into "Government" or "Private."
Private"Private Unaided Recognised" schools only, as labelled in the source. Unrecognised private schools are not part of UDISE+'s recognised-school universe and are not represented anywhere in this dashboard.
Academic yearThe selector covers every academic year from 2011–12 to 2025–26. Where a government figure was not published for a year, the value is a labelled estimate; available measures differ by year and by dataset.
Pupil–Teacher Ratio (PTR)Reported directly by the state-wise file as a single state-level figure. Not recalculated, and not available split by education level, management type or rural/urban in this data.
Students per schoolReported by the source as avg_enrolment_per_school (state total enrolment ÷ state total schools).
Zero-enrolment schoolsRecognised schools with zero students on roll in a given year, as reported by the source; excluded from PTR since the ratio is undefined at zero.
Single-teacher schoolsSchools with exactly one teacher on staff, as reported by the source.
Missing dataSource-series gaps remain unavailable in the original indicators. The separate year-wise management comparison explicitly labels its modelled values and documents the allocation method; these are not source-reported management counts.
Survey vs. administrative dataBoth source files are administrative UDISE+ counts, not sample surveys. No ASER, NAS or NSS survey data is loaded, so no learning-outcome or expenditure survey figures appear anywhere in this dashboard.

Design simplifications, stated plainly

  • No geographic map: the source files contain no state-boundary (GeoJSON) data, so the brief's clickable India map is implemented as a clickable, sortable state table with the same filtering behaviour.
  • Coverage varies by measure. Some early years contain only selected indicators; source trend lines show gaps rather than imputing values. The overview's separate national Government vs Private comparison fills every year with clearly labelled estimates when needed.
  • Observed Government vs Private management counts are available only for 2023–24 and 2024–25; the latter enrolment split is suspect. Other years in the overview are modelled from national totals and the nearest reliable management shares. The state-wise file has no management breakdown, so no state-level split is shown.

Extending this dashboard

The AY2023–24/AY2024–25 overview uses the STATEWISE and NATIONAL_MGMT records. Multi-year indicators are loaded from the cleaned master series represented by D.rows. Append verified state/year/metric/value records to that series to extend trend coverage; missing fields are not estimated.
